newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: First food contracts under UN-Iraq oil scheme set.
newsitem.headline: First food contracts under UN-Iraq oil scheme set.

text.p: The United Nations Sanctions Committee on Iraq on Thursday approved two grain contracts to Iraq worth $55 million, the first such contracts under the UN-Iraq oil-for-food scheme, UN diplomats said.
Both contracts, one for $50 million of Australian wheat, the other for $5 million of Thai rice, are for delivery on February 20.
"Approval was automatic as there was no objection raised by five o'clock, (1700 EST/0000 GMT)," said one western diplomat on the sanctions committee.

The contracts were the first food contracts to be approved under the UN-Iraq oil-for-food agreement, which allows $2 billion worth of Iraq oil sales over six months. Proceeds must be spent mostly on food.
Diplomats also said a contract to buy spare parts for Iraq's oil pipeline system was also approved. However, the second application for spare pipeline parts is still pending, they said.
